analysis.title: GS - Stankard - Eq Positioning and Key Levels - 26 Oct 2026
key_insights: CTA models forecast trend followers selling equities across all regions this week for about $23.5bn (roughly -1 standard deviation in size). CTAs are estimated long about $50bn of global equities, of which $36bn (72%) is SPX.
Base case is CTAs sell about $11.5bn of SPX this week while short-term trend remains negative.
GS Prime Brokerage: global equities were net sold for a 3rd straight week (-0.6 SDs 1-year). De-grossing accelerated, with long sales outpacing short covers 3.4 to 1.
Single stocks were net sold for a 6th straight week, driven by long sales. Macro products were net bought for the first time in 3 weeks, driven by long buys.

Staples was the most net bought global sector in dollar terms, with HFs buying at the fastest pace in 10 weeks via long buys and short covers. Real Estate and Cons Disc were also among the most net bought.
7 of 11 global sectors were net sold, led in dollar terms by TMT (Info Tech + Comm Svcs) and Energy. HFs net sold global Energy at the fastest pace in over 5 months.
US equities were net sold for a 3rd straight week (-0.9 SDs 1-year). US single stocks saw the largest de-grossing since late July.
US Industrials was among the most net sold sectors, sold for a 2nd straight week (7 of last 8) at the fastest pace in more than 6 months (-1.8 SDs 1-year).
US Staples and Real Estate were by far the most net bought US sectors. Real Estate net buying was the largest in more than 5 years (+2.4 SDs 1-year) and Staples the largest since Jul '25 (+1.8 SDs).
Fundamental L/S net leverage fell to a 1-year low of 47.0%, and US L/S net leverage fell to 43.4% (0th percentile 5-year), so hedge fund net exposure is at or near multi-year lows.

The GS Equity Fundamental L/S Performance Estimate fell -1.28% between 10/16 and 10/22 (vs MSCI World TR -0.76%), driven by beta of -0.98% and alpha of -0.30% on short side losses. The Systematic L/S estimate fell -1.26%.

Buybacks: about 27% of the index is in open window now, rising to about 50% by the end of the week. GS expects an uptick in volumes into November, seasonally the desk's second most active execution month.
Buyback execution mix is shifting slowly toward discretionary flow, at 16% discretionary vs 84% 10b5-1 plans, from 15% and 85% the prior week. Desk flows last week were 0.7x 2025 YTD ADTV.

Positioning view only: HFs net sold US Industrials at the fastest pace in more than 6 months (-1.8 SDs 1-year).
Positioning view only: HFs net sold global Energy at the fastest pace in over 5 months.
Positioning view only: US Real Estate net buying was the largest in more than 5 years (+2.4 SDs 1-year).

earnings_insights: A substantial portion of the S&P 500 reports results this week. About 27% of the index is in a buyback open window now, rising to about 50% by the end of the week as corporate windows reopen after reporting.
risk_factors: Short-term trend in SPX remains negative, which keeps CTA selling in the base case.
In the down-tape scenario CTAs would sell $60.70B of equities over 1 week and $172.52B over 1 month, much larger than the flat-tape flows.
vol_and_positioning: CTA flow forecasts over the next 1 week: flat tape sellers $23.61B ($15.01B out of the US), up tape buyers $3.60B ($7.14B out of the US), down tape sellers $60.70B ($31.23B out of the US).
CTA flow forecasts over the next 1 month: flat tape sellers $36.42B ($17.02B out of the US), up tape buyers $114.38B ($31.98B into the US), down tape sellers $172.52B ($75.34B out of the US).
SPX CTA pivot levels: short term 7717, medium term 7532, long term 7070. A 1x standard deviation market move is 1.62% in 1 week and 3.78% in 1 month.

Overall PB book gross leverage rose 0.6 pts to 312.3% (79th percentile 1-year), while net leverage fell 0.9 pts to 71.8% (3rd percentile 1-year). The L/S ratio fell 0.7% to 1.597 (3rd percentile 1-year).

Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 0.8 pts to 211.7% (63rd percentile). Beta-adjusted fundamental net leverage fell 3.5 pts to 60.4% (1-year low) and beta-adjusted gross fell 1.9 pts to 226.5% (25th percentile).
US L/S gross leverage rose 2.2 pts to 216.1% (64th percentile 1-year). The US Fundamental long/short ratio fell 0.7% to 1.503 (0th percentile 5-year).
Staples gross/net allocations in the global Prime book are 4.6%/1.4%, in the 70th/57th percentiles vs the past year and the 23rd/13th percentiles vs the past five years.
